observations: Black upholstered salon chair with a circular chrome base.
Wooden armrests with a polished reddish-brown finish.
Chrome footrest bar attached to the seat frame.
The backrest is partially covered in a thin, clear plastic protective wrap which appears torn in photo 1.
A hydraulic foot pedal is visible at the base in photo 1.
The chrome base shows some surface smudges and dust.
The chair is stored in a cluttered indoor environment.

claims.evidence: The plastic wrap is present but messy and torn; the chrome base shows smudges suggesting it has been handled or stored unprotected.
This typically implies hydraulic lift and reclining features, which cannot be tested through static photos.

risks.risk: Hydraulic pump may be seized or leaking fluid.
risks.proof: A video showing the chair being pumped to full height and then released.

risks.risk: Reclining mechanism (if present) may be broken.
risks.proof: A photo of the chair in a fully reclined position.

risks.risk: Upholstery damage hidden under the plastic wrap.
risks.proof: Photos of the backrest with the plastic completely removed.

proof_requests: Video of the hydraulic pump lifting and lowering the chair.
Photos of the backrest with the plastic wrap removed.
Photo of the chair in a reclined position if it has that feature.
response.reason: The item is a standard hydraulic salon chair. It can be priced as a used, non-reclining unit with a non-functional pump as the worst-case scenario.
